questions.q: In the following reaction, $4P + 3KOH + 3{H}_{2}O \to 3K{H}_{2}P{O}_{2} + P{H}_{3}$
options: P is both oxidized as well as reduced
questions.solution:
$4\overset{0}{P} + 3KOH + 3{H}_{2}O \to 3{KH}_{2}\overset{+ 1}{P}{O}_{2} + \overset{- 3}{P}{H}_{3}$

It is a disproportionation reaction. Here P atom changes oxidation number zero to +1 and zero to -3. Hence, P is both oxidized as well as reduced

questions.q: $50 \mathrm{~cm}^{3}$ of $0.2 \mathrm{~N} \mathrm{HCl}$ is titrated against $0.1 \mathrm{~N}\mathrm{NaOH}$ solution. The titration is discontinued after adding $50 \mathrm{~cm}^{3}$ of $\mathrm{NaOH}$. The remaining titration is completed by adding $0.5 \mathrm{~N} \mathrm{KOH}$. The volume of $\mathrm{KOH}$ required for completing the titration is
questions.solution:
When $0.1 \mathrm{~N} \mathrm{NaOH}$ is used, $\begin{gathered} \mathrm{N}_{1} \mathrm{~V}_{1}=\mathrm{N}_{2} \mathrm{~V}_{2}$\\
$\text { (For HCl) }$\\
$\text { (For NaOH) }$\\
0.2 $\mathrm{~N} \times \mathrm{V}_{1}=$50 $\times$0.1 $\mathrm{~N}$\\
$\mathrm{~V}_{1}=\frac{50 \times 0.1}{0.2}=$25 $\mathrm{~cm}^{3}
\end{gathered}$When $0.5 \mathrm{~N} \mathrm{KOH}$ is used, $\begin{aligned} \mathrm{N}_{1} \mathrm{~V}_{1}=$& $\mathrm{N}_{3} \mathrm{~V}_{3}$\\
$\text { (For remaining HCl) }$&($\text { For KOH})$\\
0.2 $\mathrm{~N} \times$25 &=0.5 $\mathrm{~N} \times \mathrm{V}_{3}$\\
$\mathrm{~V}_{3}$&=$\frac{0.2 \times 25}{0.5}$\\
=& 10 $\mathrm{~cm}^{3}
\end{aligned}$

When $250 \mathrm{~mL}$ of $0.1 \mathrm{M} \mathrm{KI}$ solution is mixed with $250 \mathrm{~mL}$ of $0.02 \mathrm{M}\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ in basic medium, what is the number of moles of $\mathrm{I}_2$ formed?
questions.solution:
$\begin{array}{r}\lceil\text {-factor }=1 \longrightarrow \\ \mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}+\mathrmI^{-} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{MnO}_2+\mathrm{I}_2 \\ \bigsqcup_{n \text {-factor }=3}^{\rightleftharpoons}\end{array}
Number of milli equivalents of
$\mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}=0.02 \times 3 \times 250=15$
Number of milli equivalents of
$\mathrm{I}_2=0.1 \times 1 \times 250=25$
Thus, here $\mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}$is limiting reagent.
$\therefore$ Number of milli equivalents of $\mathrm{I}_2$ formed $=$
Number of milli equivalent of $\mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}=15$
or number of equivalent of $\mathrm{I}_2$ formed
=\frac{15}{1000}=$0.$015\begin{aligned}
\therefore \text { Number of moles of } \mathrm{I}}_{2} \text { formed } & $=\frac{0.015}{2}$\\
& =0.0075
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A compound contains three elements X, Y and Z. The oxidation number of X, Y and Z are $+ 3, + 5$ and $- 2$ respectively. The possible formula of the compound is
questions.solution:
The sum of all oxidation values must be equal to zero. Let, number of atoms of X, Y and Z are respectively a, b and c.

Then, $( + 3 ) ext{a} + ( + 5 ) ext{b} + ( - 2 ) ext{c} = 0$

Or

$3 ext{a} + 5 ext{b} - 2 ext{c} = 0$

Now, putting values of a, b and c for all the given options, which will give sum equal to zero, will be our formula.

(a) For, ${ ext{X}}_{2} ext{Y} ext{Z}$

$ ext{a} = 2$

$ ext{b} = 1$

$ ext{c} = 1$

Thus, $3 ext{a} + 5 ext{b} - 2 ext{c} = 0$

$3 imes 2 + 5 - 2 e 0$

(b) For, $ ext{X} ext{Y}{ ext{Z}}_{3}$

$ ext{a} = 1, ext{b} = 1, ext{c} = 3$

$3 ext{a} + 5 ext{b} - 2 ext{c} = 0$

$3 + 5 - 6 e 0$

(c) ${ ext{X}}_{3}{( ext{Y}{ ext{Z}}_{4} )}_{3}$

$ ext{a} = 3, ext{b} = 3, ext{c} = 12$

$3 ext{a} + 5 ext{b} - 2 ext{c} = 0$

$( 3 imes 3 + 5 imes 3 ) - ( 2 imes 12 ) = 0$

$9 + 15 - 24$

$24 - 24 = 0$

(d) ${ ext{X}}_{2}{ ext{Y}}_{2} ext{Z}$

$ ext{a} = 2, ext{b} = 2, ext{c} = 1$

$3 ext{a} + 5 ext{b} - 2 ext{c} = 0$

$( 3 imes 2 ) + ( 5 imes 2 ) - ( 2 imes 1 ) = 0$

$6 + 10 - 2 e 0$

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.q: Which of the following is disproportionation reaction?
questions.solution:
Reactions in which the same substance is oxidized as well as reduced are called disproportionation reaction. Writing the oxidation number of each element above its symbol in the given reactions.

$\overset{+ 4}{C}\overset{+ 1}{{H}_{4}} + 2{{O}_{2}}^{0} \to \overset{+ 4}{C}\overset{- 2}{{O}_{2}} + 2\overset{+ 1}{{H}_{2}}\overset{- 2}{O}$

$\overset{- 4}{C}\overset{+ 1}{{H}_{4}} + 4{{Cl}_{2}}^{0} \to \overset{+ 4}{C}C{l}_{4} +4\overset{+ 1}{H} \overset{- 1}{C} l$

$2{F}_{2}^{0} + 2\overset{- 2}{O}\overset{+ 1}{H^{-}} \to 2\overset{- 1}{F} + \overset{+ 2}{O}{F}_{2}^{- 1} + \overset{- 1}{{H}_{2}}\overset{- 2}{O}$

$2\overset{+ 4}{N}\overset{- 2}{{O}_{2}} + 2\overset{- 2}{O}\overset{+ 1}{H^{-}} \to \overset{+ 3}{N}\overset{- 2}{{{O}_{2}}^{-}} + \overset{+ 5}{N}\overset{- 2}{{{O}_{3}}^{-}} + \overset{+ 1}{{H}_{2}}\overset{- 2}{O}$

Thus, in the reaction of $N{O}_{2}$ and $OH^{-}, N$ is both oxidized as well as reduced. Hence, the oxidation number increases from $+ 4$ in $N{O}_{2}$ to $+ 5$ in $N{O}_{3}^{-}$ and decreases from $+ 4$ in $N{O}_{2}$ to $+ 3$ in $N{O}_{2}^{-} .$

questions.q: $1g$~of an impure sample of magnesium carbonate (containing no thermally decomposable impurities) on complete thermal decomposition gave~$0 . 44g$& of carbon dioxide gas. The percentage of impurity in the sample is
questions.solution:
Consider,

${MgCO}_{3} \to MgO + {CO}_{2} ↑$

${MgCO}_{3}$:~\left(1 \times 24\right) + \left(1 \times 12\right) + \left(3 \times 16\right) = 84g$

${CO}_{2}$:~

\left(1 \times 12\right) + \left(2 \times 16\right) = 44g$

$100 %$~pure $84g$~${MgCO}_{3}$ on heating gives $44g$~${CO}_{2}$

Given that~$1g$ ~of ${MgCO}_{3}$~on heating gives $0 . 44g$~${CO}_{2}$

Therefore, $84g$~${MgCO}_{3}$~sample on heating gives $36 . 96g$~${CO}_{2}$

Percentage of purity of the sample =~$\dfrac{36 . 96gof{CO}_{2}}{44gof{CO}_{2}} \times 100 % = 84 %$

Percentage of impurity =~$16 %$
